Corridor #2 - begins at its westerly end from an interchange located at existing I-94 approximately midway between Grange Avenue and Layton Avenue. This freeway access interchange to I-94 would be located just south of Edgerton Avenue which would be 1-1/2 miles north of the College Avenue Interchange and 1/2 mile south of the directional interchange at Layton Avenue. Because of its proximity to the directional interchange at Layton Avenue another interchange could create serious traffic operational difficulities resulting from short weaving movements between the ramps.

The area is also highly developed with residential properties.
The corridor extends southeasterly from I-94 and Edgerton Avenue to 9th Street. At the time this corridor was proposed for a freeway facility its location would have traversed a vacant 40 acre wooded area lying south of Edgerton Avenue between I-94 and 13th Street. This tract has since been converted into condominium and apartment type homes. Presently, a freeway facility located within this area would severly disrupt this housing.
The corridor's diagonal alignment would also leave triangular pieces of land which may result in inefficient use of the land. The area from 13th Street to 9th Street is predominately agricultural type lands and is zoned for light industry. After crossing the C.M. St. P. & P. Railroad the corridor proceeds easterly with an alignment that would be parallel to Grange Avenue. The corridor would be north of an abandoned quarry area that is principally used for truck storage and dump area.
